title: Zero error of a correct randomized tree
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite alphabet, let $\alpha$ be an output type with decidable equality, and let $n$ be a natural number. If a randomized decision tree computes $f:(\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\Omega)\to\alpha$ correctly for every seed, then its error probability under any probability law on $\Omega$ is zero.
hypotheses_covered: The output type $\alpha$ has decidable equality
The randomized tree has a finite nonempty seed space with a probability law
Every seed’s deterministic tree computes $f$ correctly
